video:video.video:title: Why your phone puts you across the street
video:video.video:description: A fictional pickup explains reflected satellite signals, an uncertain map dot and a practical way to agree where to meet.

video:video.video:title: AI agents need shared notes, and a way to check them
video:video.video:description: A fictional repair workshop explains reusable agent knowledge, context checks and a boundary for private project information.

video:video.video:title: Tesla says Roadster can fly: three questions to ask
video:video.video:description: An illustrated hangar explains thrust and separates a manufacturer claim from availability and public-road approval.

video:video.video:title: How cold outdoor air can help warm a home
video:video.video:description: A fictional home and an illustrative energy balance explain how a heat pump moves heat.

video:video.video:title: AI agents: ability is not authority
video:video.video:description: A fictional invoice explains reading, drafting and approval boundaries in business AI.

video:video.video:title: Same rent, different service-charge bill
video:video.video:description: A fictional Dubai property comparison separates advertised rent from cash remaining after one recurring cost.

video:video.video:title: The confident answer from the old price list
video:video.video:description: In a fictional hotel, Leila asks an AI assistant for a meeting-room quote. A fluent answer appears. Before sending it, she spots the problem: its supporting sheet is an old version. This is a teaching scenario, not a report of an actual hotel or product test.

video:video.video:title: The money has a project name
video:video.video:description: Fictional buyer Rami sees a beautiful model of an unfinished building. His useful question is not only what it will look like, but which records support the payment instructions. No real project or account is represented here.

video:video.video:title: The button moved. The AI did not notice.
video:video.video:description: In a fictional parcel studio, Nora asks an AI helper to prepare a label. A panel moves before the click arrives. The cursor moves, but the label is still missing. This illustrates a failure possibility; it is not an observed shipment or product test.

video:video.video:title: Next door is not always comparable
video:video.video:description: Fictional buyer Mina places two neighbouring flats on a comparison rail. One card is an asking price; the other records an older agreed sale. Neither card becomes identical evidence merely because the doors are close. No actual property, price or valuation is represented.

video:video.video:title: A beautiful building model can still be out of date
video:video.video:description: In a fictional office, Omar sees a polished building model while a room feels wrong. The useful question is not how realistic the model looks. It is which physical asset the data describes and when that data was observed.

video:video.video:title: The document tried to become the boss
video:video.video:description: A fictional theatre shows why reading a document should not let it take over an AI assistant. A smaller tool set, checks on incoming content and human approval points can limit the damage from a misleading instruction.
